verdicts.strongest_argument: The consensus number itself is the hunter's own published source (MarketBeat/DailyPolitical, 2026-08-31: $(0.27) and $237.985M), and every one of the 'building blocks' it is measured against was disclosed by management on 2026-06-24 and reported the same day: data centre $80M to ~$130M, North American automotive $182M to 'close to $200 million', FY27 sales $1,025-1,075M. So the arithmetic is a re-arrangement of public inputs, not new information. Worse, the arithmetic breaks when you respect the rest of the same disclosure. CFO Kowalchik said on that call 'we expect a lighter first quarter driven by typical seasonality' with sales ramping into a stronger second half. Consensus $238M is 22.7% of the $1,050M guide midpoint, versus Q1 FY26's 23.6% share of FY26's $1,019M actual - i.e. consensus already encodes a lighter-than-normal Q1, exactly as guided. The hunter's ~$257M would put Q1 at 24-25% of the year while H2 is supposed to be stronger, which only fits at or above the very top of the guided range. The building blocks are also gross of the offsets management folded into a +0.6% to +5.5% total-sales guide: EV program roll-offs, Interface weakness, the dataMate divestiture ($16M sale, closed after Q3 FY26) and the Harwood Heights disposal. Finally, the two-quarter 'consensus is 7% low' pattern is cherry-picked - Q2 FY26 revenue beat consensus by 4.6% ($246.9M vs $236.13M) and the stock still fell 10.9% the next day on an EPS miss, and StockStory's own MEI copy states MEI 'has missed Wall Street's revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years'. Revenue versus a four-analyst consensus is demonstrably not this stock's reaction driver; EBITDA and guidance are. Residual novelty: nobody has written up 'this thin consensus sits below the disclosed run-rate', and the calendar's rogue $(0.47) single estimate does show the sell-side print here is unreliable. That is worth something, but not much, and not 7%.

Q2 FY26 revenue of $246.9M beat the $236.13M consensus by 4.6% and the stock fell anyway on a $(0.28) vs $(0.25) EPS miss - the mechanism this finding relies on failing in the most recent comparable case.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Spot 18.705 after a 23.87% 20-day run-up sits at 85% of the published $22 average target and above the $16 low, so the tape is already leaning toward the company's own numbers being achievable. Baseline carries no reaction history (records bug), but I reconstructed it from Yahoo daily bars: the last four prints moved -10.9% (2025-12-04), -11.8% (2026-03-06), +12.2% (2025-09-10) and +37.5% (2026-06-25). Every one of those was decided by EBITDA/guidance, not by revenue versus a four-name consensus, which caps what a revenue-only edge can be worth here.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A sell-side revenue estimate for Q1 FY27 sourced to a named broker at or above $250M, or evidence that Methode's Q1 datacentre busbar shipments alone exceeded the ~$32M/quarter run-rate implied by the $130M FY27 guide.
verdicts.notes: Consensus question the brief asked me to settle: the published figure is $(0.27) on $237.99M (MarketBeat aggregate over ~4 analysts, corroborated by stockanalysis' 4-analyst FY27 panel and a $(0.41) full-year FY27 EPS consensus). The calendar's $(0.47) on a single estimate is an outlier and should not be treated as the priced expectation. Caveat: MarketBeat's EPS series for MEI is inconsistent with the adjusted basis the market trades on - it recorded Q4 FY26 as $(0.30) versus $(0.11) 'consensus' while the adjusted print was +$0.01 versus $(0.09) and the stock rose 37.5%.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component of this is front-page wire copy, and more damagingly, it is the exact narrative the last 24% of this stock's move is made of. Amazon/Alphabet/Meta's 2026 capex raises were the dominant tech story of late July and are the hunter's own CNBC source of 2026-07-28. GM's second 2026 EBIT-adjusted guidance raise was a PRNewswire release at 06:30 ET on 2026-07-21 carried by Morningstar, Barchart, Yahoo and TradingView. 'Methode is an AI-datacentre busbar supplier levered to hyperscaler capex' is not a discovery in September 2026 - it is why the stock went from $13.09 to $18.00 on 2026-06-25 (+37.5%) when management first put the $130M datacentre number on the tape, and why Craig-Hallum initiated Buy with a $30 target on 2026-08-25, moving the stock +14.4% in one session. The observation that 800VDC is excluded from guidance is itself a management statement on the 2026-06-24 call ('none of that is in our guide'), reported at the time, so the 'free option' framing is the sell-side's framing, not a discovery. The one thing the finding gets right that is genuinely underdrawn is the timing asymmetry - the guide is dated 25 June and the macro datapoints post-date it - but with the stock up 43% off the 2026-08-24 close of $14.03 and the put skew nonetheless bid at +14.2 vol points, the market is not treating the guide as a ceiling. It is treating it as stale in the same direction the hunter is.

The stock has round-tripped from $14.03 (2026-08-24) to $18.705 in six sessions with no company fundamental release in the window - that move is the market paying up for precisely this thesis. atm_iv_pct 106.5 with a $22 average target and a $30 high means the upside case is already funded.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A company-specific datapoint dated after 25 June that is not the macro tape - an award announcement, a named hyperscaler program, or a channel check on Methode's own busbar shipment volumes.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The $22.5M of customer recoveries is not a detail buried in an exhibit - it is in the second sentence of the company's own 2026-06-24 headline release ('net sales were $298.1 million ... including $22.5 million of customer recoveries') and was repeated in essentially every piece of coverage, including StockTitan, GlobeNewswire, Yahoo, Investing.com and the Motley Fool piece explaining the 40% jump. 'The recovery activity is largely done' is a direct quote from the same call. And the sequential collapse the finding calls 'the year's worst sequential optics' is already the published expectation: consensus of $237.99M against a $298.1M actual is a -20% sequential print that the sell-side has written down, and management pre-announced it as 'a lighter first quarter driven by typical seasonality'. A decline the company guided and the consensus already models is not a surprise; it is the base case. The residual is the second-order point that ex-recoveries EBITDA was only ~$7.9M ($26.9M less the ~$19M management said flowed to earnings), so the sequential EBITDA optic is uglier than the revenue optic - but that adjustment is also published (see MEI-2#0), and it is the same arithmetic. The '52-week high' framing is the only part with real force, and it is the baseline restated: pct_from_52w_high is -3.68 and the put skew is already bid at +14.2 vol points, so the market is paying for the risk that ugly optics into a high gets sold.

DeGaynor: 'The recovery activity is largely done'; of ~$45M negotiated, ~$23M was recognised in FY26 revenue with ~$19M flowing to earnings and the remaining ~$22M spread over three to four years; CFO guides 'a lighter first quarter'.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: skew_25d_vol_points +14.23 with priced_direction_lean 'downside paid' and put/call OI 0.91: the market is already paying a premium for the scenario this finding describes. pct_from_52w_high -3.68 confirms the 'into a 52-week high' setup is visible to everyone. Reconstructed history shows MEI does sell off hard on bad EBITDA optics (-10.9% on 2025-12-04, -11.8% on 2026-03-06), so the reaction function is real - but it is exactly what a 106.5% ATM IV and a 14-point put skew are pricing.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the four-analyst consensus does NOT strip the recoveries - e.g. a broker Q1 EBITDA estimate anywhere near a $26.9M-style run-rate - which would mean the sequential fall is genuinely unmodelled.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The two anchoring documents are both public company releases from a year ago, and they were wire-distributed: the 2025-08-21 pre-announcement of a 3 September date (Nasdaq press release) and the 2025-09-03 reschedule notice (GlobeNewswire, carried by the Globe and Mail, Manila Times and Yahoo Finance), followed by the 2025-09-09 release with the beat. I confirmed the reschedule notice does indeed give no reason - two sentences, no explanation - so that part of the claim holds. But this is the weakest-mechanism finding in the set on three counts. First, the magnitude is wrong: close-to-close on 2025-09-04 was $7.65 to $7.02, i.e. -8.2%, not -11.4% (Yahoo daily bars). Second, the follow-through cuts against the bear read - the actual 2025-09-09 print produced +12.2% on 2025-09-10, so the pattern the finding documents ends in an up move, and the 'low bar' half of the claim is the same argument as MEI-1#0. Third, and decisively, it is a low-probability tail with a shrinking window: it is 16:10 UTC with the release a few hours away and no 8-K or notice has appeared; last year's notice hit at roughly 20:05 UTC on the scheduled day, so there is residual window, but a single non-recurring precedent with no stated cause and no visible 2026 analogue (no restatement, no auditor change, no material-weakness disclosure I can find) is not a probability the market should be paying much for. Where I concede: the -8.2% reschedule reaction and the +12.2% print reaction are nowhere in this baseline (history.n is 0, a records bug), nobody has written 'watch for a repeat', and the market is genuinely not being shown that base rate. That is why this is not an 80.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the strongest arithmetic in the set and it was published on the day of the guide, by more than one outlet, in a larger version than the hunter's. TipRanks' Q4 FY26 report page, dated 2026-06-24, states the FY27 guide of '$72-82 million (implying a ~7.0-7.6% margin; ~13% growth vs FY2026 and ~82% growth ex-refinements/recoveries)'. Investing.com's coverage of Methode's own Q4 FY26 slide deck puts the same figure at ~51% adjusted EBITDA growth excluding FY26 portfolio actions and customer recoveries. The hunter's +47% to +67% sits inside that published bracket. And the input is management's own disclosure on the call - ~$19M of the ~$23M revenue-recognised recoveries flowed to adjusted EBITDA - not something dug out of the exhibit. I verified the rest of the arithmetic and it is all correct: Q3 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.1% on $233.7M net sales, so $7.3M; $26.9M less ~$19M is $7.9M on $275.6M underlying, i.e. 2.9%, flat with Q3; FY26 $68.2M less $19M is $49.2M. Correct, material, and already in the sell-side's own framing of the guide. The company itself appears to have presented the ex-recoveries comparison in the Q4 deck, which makes this the definition of restating published guidance. What is not priced is a narrower question - whether Q1 specifically shows the first instalment of that ~50-60% ramp - but that is a forecast, not a finding.

Management quantifies the recoveries: ~$23M recognised in FY26 revenue with ~$19M flowing through to adjusted EBITDA.
Q3 FY26 net sales $233.7M with a 3.1% adjusted EBITDA margin - the $7.3M base of the sequential comparison, public since March.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The 2026-06-25 reaction is the evidence: the stock rose 37.5% on the print that contained both the recoveries and the ex-recoveries reconciliation, so the market saw the adjustment and bought anyway. The +14.23-point put skew shows the residual risk of the ramp not showing up is being paid for. No baseline history to lean on (n=0), but the four reconstructed print reactions - +12.2%, -10.9%, -11.8%, +37.5% - confirm EBITDA/guidance is what this stock trades on, so this is the right axis; it is just already on it.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This finding is the baseline. run_up_5d_pct is 16.54 and run_up_20d_pct is 23.87 in the sealed file; the Craig-Hallum move is the hunter's own cited StockStory/FinancialContent article of 2026-08-25; the price targets ($16 low, $22 average, $30 high) are on stockanalysis' public forecast page; and 'the company guided Q1 to be seasonally weak' is the CFO's own sentence from 2026-06-24. Every element is either in the sealed baseline the hunters were handed or on a public quote page. I did verify the structural observation and it holds - 5 sessions back from the 18.705 close is exactly the 2026-08-25 close of $16.05, so the 16.5% run-up is indeed entirely post-initiation, and I found no company release in the window other than the 26 August date notice. But an unexplained momentum run-up into a guided-weak print is the most legible setup on a screen, and the option market has already responded to it: the ATM IV is 106.5% and the 25-delta put skew is +14.23 vol points with the baseline itself labelling the priced direction 'downside paid'. Two small corrections: the initiation day's close-to-close move was +14.40% (Yahoo: $14.03 to $16.05), the +14.9% being intraday; and the $22 average target is stale against Craig-Hallum's $30, which is now the high end of a $16-$30 range.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I verified the claim and it is factually correct: the SemiAnalysis 800VDC piece of 2026-05-26 does not mention Methode Electronics and does name TE Connectivity for the standardized busbars in the Diablo 400 specification. But the mechanism does not reach tonight's print, and that is the whole problem. 800VDC is not in FY27 guidance by management's own explicit statement on 2026-06-24 - 'none of that is in our guide' - so no Q1 FY27 revenue line, no FY27 guide component, and no consensus number moves on it. Nor does the piece contradict what the market is actually paying for: the $80M-to-$130M datacentre ramp is existing vendor-managed busbar volume with hyperscalers moving from spot buys to multi-week EDI, which is a different business from being a named supplier in an OCP rack specification, and TE being named for Diablo 400 busbars does not exclude Methode from other hyperscaler programs. Publication-wise this is genuinely awkward to score: SemiAnalysis is a paid newsletter, so it is not wire copy, but it is the single most-read AI-supply-chain publication among exactly the specialist holders who bid this stock from $14.03 to $18.705, and the piece predates the June guide by a month and the Craig-Hallum initiation by three. The specialists read it and initiated at $30 anyway. What is unpublished is the specific juxtaposition - MEI's 800VDC option value versus its absence from the teardown - and I found nobody drawing it. That is worth a middling number, capped hard by the fact that the only channel to tonight's outcome is whether management oversells 800VDC on tomorrow morning's call.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Names TE Connectivity for standardized busbars in the Diablo 400 specification and does not mention Methode Electronics anywhere - the finding's factual base, published three months ago.
DeGaynor: 'When we reference the future technology and the 800-volt architectures, none of that is in our guide' - the company has already told the market 800VDC contributes nothing to FY27.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None that bears directly on 800VDC. The 23.87% 20-day run-up and the $30 Craig-Hallum target show the market is paying something for the AI-datacentre option, but that option is anchored on the disclosed $130M busbar ramp rather than on 800VDC rack content, which management removed from the guide. No move in the baseline coincides with 2026-05-26.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A specific, dated hyperscaler or ODM design win going to a named competitor on a program Methode had publicly claimed, or management quantifying 800VDC revenue on tomorrow's call in a way the teardown contradicts.

interactions: Three real interactions. (1) MEI-1#2 and MEI-2#0 are the same finding computed two ways off the same document: both strip the customer recoveries out of Q4 FY26 to expose ~$7.9M of underlying EBITDA (MEI-1#2's 'single-digit-millions' is arithmetically identical to MEI-2#0's 'ex-recoveries Q4 margin ~2.9%'), and both trace to the 2026-06-24 8-K exhibit plus the same call quote. They must not be counted as two independent pieces of evidence; the ex-recoveries adjustment was published by TipRanks and by Investing.com's slide coverage on the guide date, which prices both at once. (2) MEI-1#0 and MEI-2#1 are mirror images resting on the same published number - MEI-1#0 argues the $237.99M consensus is too low, MEI-2#1 argues the stock has run into a quarter the company guided weak. Both are true statements about the same setup and they largely cancel: consensus at 22.7% of the guide midpoint is what a guided-lighter Q1 looks like, so 'consensus is low' and 'the quarter is weak' are the same fact seen from two sides. (3) MEI-1#1 and MEI-2#2 contradict each other directly on the datacentre thesis. MEI-1#1 treats 800VDC as unpriced upside optionality; MEI-2#2 treats Methode's absence from the SemiAnalysis 800VDC teardown as unpriced downside. Both cite the same management exclusion of 800VDC from guidance as support, which means at most one of them can be adding information, and in fact neither reaches the Q1 FY27 numbers because the excluded line is excluded from both consensus and guidance. Separately, a records note for the caller: the brief's warning is correct and I reconstructed the missing history from Yahoo daily bars - the last four MEI prints moved +12.2% (2025-09-10), -10.9% (2025-12-04), -11.8% (2026-03-06) and +37.5% (2026-06-25), median absolute 12.0%, and Q3 FY25 in March 2025 fell 28.4%. This is a violently reactive name, not a quiet one, and the baseline's event_implied_move_pct of 7.4 looks understated against both that record and the 18.44% front-expiry straddle; the derivation subtracts a 20-day realised vol that is itself inflated by the pre-print momentum run. Any finding worth less than about 3 percentage points is noise against this distribution, which is why I have sized nothing above 8.
